ctx.x: She'd come to the Golden Leather?

Sure, Martha Ray was dead, it was the regular as that finger to her, get right down that mic and go to singing. She could sing too, partner. And first thing I know, that woman was gone, to California. I said, what's been happening here now? I said, man, they're going into business. Show the real picture. I said, well, I betcha, maybe I know she wouldn't know nothing about me. And I tell you, girl, we started out with us, couldn't sing one song. She gives our name June Richmond now. But her first name is Burdette…
What about Jimmy Wade? Did you work with him?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: The only guy that made records was Tiny Pong, Al Wynn, Jimmy Wade. He was a big chief.

ctx.x: Nice piano player. When you played with Jelly Roll did you ever make any records with him? No, I didn't.

He didn't make no while I was with him. He had made some before I got with him. But I don't think he made no more after that. Because he died right after I got out of the band, me and Swayze. He didn't live long. But I heard all his records, Dr. Jazz and all that kind of stuff. But I didn't make any with him. He never made any records? The only guy that made records was Tiny Pong, Al Wynn, Jimmy Wade. He was a big chief. And what this guy named in New York, uh, the trombones. He's an Indian. Big chief. Oh, you…
Yeah, Bunk was there that year too. The Bunk sure was.

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Well, Jimmy Wade had some fellas, no you asked me that once before Dick, but I swear I can't remember them fellas. I can't remember.

ctx.x: Who was in Jimmy Wade's band?
Well, Jimmy Wade had some fellas, no you asked me that once before Dick, but I swear I can't remember them fellas. I can't remember.
Maybe they just come back to you in the meantime.
